packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-12 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind; no outside source consulted, no identification attempted)

Exposure note: none. Only the images and PROMPT.md of this packet were read.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 and image-004 are overviews of the two sides of one horizontal parchment strip
  (c. 19 x 5.5 cm by the ruler; label "A"), cut across the lower part of a bifolium: a vertical
  fold runs down the middle, sewing holes/slits along the lower edge and at the fold, and a
  broad empty lower margin. The upper edge is a cut through a line of writing.
- Main text: small gothic bookhand in black ink, two columns per page, only the last 9-10 lines
  of each column preserved. Side 1 (image-001): left page has two columns (first one cut at its
  left edge); right page has only the last 3 lines of one column (the column ended higher up)
  and, further right, a block of c. 11 lines in a different, smaller cursive hand and browner
  ink - an added note filling blank space. Side 2 (image-004): left page is filled by a long
  note in a cursive hand (16 lines, full width, written in two campaigns: the lower 6 lines are
  larger and darker); right page has two columns of the main bookhand (second cut at right).
- No rubrics, running titles, coloured initials or interlinear glosses visible. One paragraph
  mark (pen-drawn bracket) in the margin of side 1, column b, line 5. Biblical citation tags occur
  in-line ("i. R(e)g.", "ys.").
- Tentative interpretation: main text is homiletic/distinction-style prose with numbered points
  ("p(ri)mo mutat", "Sexto mutat") and repeated key verbs ("expedit, condit, dat, redimit,
  reconciliat"); the cursive blocks are later additions, the one on side 2 a narrative note.

2. AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
Read: all four main-hand column ends and the 3-line column end; the lower six lines of the
cursive note on side 2; parts of the cursive note on side 1. Largely unread: the upper ten lines
of the cursive note on side 2 (image-005 L1-10) and several lines of the side-1 note - too small
and blurred at this resolution; a higher-resolution crop of those would be needed.

3. TRANSCRIPTION
("[..]" = letters lost at a cut edge; not supplied.)

4. LIMITATIONS
- Only the bottom 9-10 lines of each column survive, so no column gives 15+ consecutive lines;
  the spans above are complete for what is preserved of the main hand. The order of the pages
  within the original quire (which side/leaf comes first) is not determinable from the strip.
- Main-hand readings are fair in columns a, x, y and in the lower half of column b; column b
  L3-L6 are doubtful. Cursive additions are small and blurred: only the lower part of the side-2
  note is reasonably read; the rest is fragmentary and marked as such.
- Overlaps: the 3-line column end appears in both image-002 and image-003; the line ends of the
  side-2 note appear at the left edge of image-006.
